issues.legal_issue: Possession of acquired land may be established through official records and the circumstances of a large public acquisition, resulting in vesting even without proof of the owner’s personal physical dispossession.
material_facts: The land was acquired as part of a large tract for a planned development scheme, and an award was made.
The acquisition officer referred the dispute over compensation and deposited the compensation in court.
The acquisition officer’s record showed delivery of possession of the acquired land to the public housing body.
The scheme was developed on the acquired tract, with many houses constructed and the disputed land set apart for a public park.
The claimant had acknowledged the public body’s title in a letter requesting an alternative site, and there was no evidence that he resisted the taking of possession.
issues.conclusion: Possession of the disputed land was taken and delivered to the public body; the land consequently vested free from encumbrances, and the claimant’s contrary claim of continuing title could not succeed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11, 16 and 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, following an award and the taking of possession, the land vests in the State free from encumbrances; compensation disputed by claimants is deposited and referred as required. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act permits a presumption that official acts were regularly performed. Taking possession need not invariably involve physical dispossession of every occupant or physical occupation of every part of a large tract; a memorandum or Panchnama made by the acquisition officer in the presence of witnesses is an accepted mode. The approach must be pragmatic and depend on the nature and circumstances of the land. The Court considered Balwant Narayan Bhagde v. M.D. Bhagwat, (1975) Supp. SCR 250, including its discussion of the modes of taking possession, but did not treat any one method as an absolute rule.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and award_made and compensation_dispute_referred_or_deposited and official_possession_record_and_delivery and (large_tract_public_scheme or claimant_acknowledged_public_title)

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The dispute arises from a proceeding to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.award_made: The acquisition officer made an award for the acquired land.
predicates.compensation_dispute_referred_or_deposit: The acquisition officer referred a dispute concerning compensation or deposited the compensation in court.
predicates.official_possession_record_and_delivery: The acquisition officer recorded the taking of possession and delivered the land to the public body.
predicates.large_tract_public_scheme: The land formed part of a large tract being developed under a public scheme.
predicates.claimant_acknowledged_public_title: The claimant acknowledged the public body’s title or acted inconsistently with a claim that title remained with him.
predicates.acquired_land_vested_in_public_authority: The acquired land vested in the public authority after possession was taken.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding includes an award and the circumstances and official evidence show possession was taken and delivered, the acquired land vests in the public authority.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose interest in land has been divested by acquisition cannot obtain an injunction restraining the public authority that holds the land as owner.
material_facts: The claimant brought a suit for perpetual injunction, asserting title to and possession of the disputed land.
The land had been acquired, possession had been taken and delivered to the public housing body, and the land was held for a public scheme and park.
The claimant’s claim of continuing title was inconsistent with his acknowledgment of the public body’s title and request for an alternative site.
issues.conclusion: The injunction could not be granted against the public body as the true owner; the judgments granting it were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Once possession of acquired land has been taken, Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides for vesting free from encumbrances. A trespasser cannot claim an injunction against the true owner, and a claimant whose title has been divested cannot obtain an injunction against the public authority in which the land is vested.

predicates.suit_for_perpetual_injunction: The claimant brought a suit seeking a perpetual injunction against interference with land.
predicates.land_taken_and_delivered_for_public_sche: The acquisition officer took possession of the land and delivered it to a public body for a public scheme.
predicates.claimant_has_no_remaining_title: The claimant’s interest in the land had been divested and the claimant had no remaining title to it.
predicates.injunction_unavailable_against_true_owne: An injunction cannot be granted against the public body that holds the land as true owner.

issues.definition: A claimant seeking a perpetual injunction cannot obtain it against the true owner when the land was taken and delivered for a public scheme and the claimant has no remaining title.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to mutate acquired land in revenue records or separately register it does not defeat the public authority’s acquired title.
material_facts: The disputed land was acquired under the statutory process and an award was made.
The public authority’s name had not been entered in the revenue records, and the land had not been separately registered in its name.
The acquisition officer had recorded possession and delivered the land to the public body.
issues.conclusion: The absence of mutation or separate registration did not invalidate the public authority’s title to the acquired land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 exempts land acquired under the Act from registration. The Court held that mutation in revenue records was unnecessary for the public authority’s title to the acquired land.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The dispute concerns land acquired through a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.acquisition_award_made: An award was made for the acquired land.
predicates.land_not_mutated_or_separately_registere: The public authority’s name was not entered in the revenue records or separately registered as owner of the acquired land.
predicates.absence_of_mutation_or_registration_does: The absence of mutation or separate registration does not defeat the public authority’s title to the acquired land.

issues.definition: When land has been acquired and an award has been made, failure to mutate or separately register it does not defeat the acquired title.
